course_name_en: Introduction to Electrical and Electronics Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Possess sufficient background in Mathematics, Science, and Electrical-Electronics engineering subjects; have the ability to use theoretical and applied knowledge in these areas together for engineering solutions.
Be able to use the knowledge and skills acquired in Electrical and Electronics Engineering to solve problems; apply analytical and strategic thinking.
Establish the connection between engineering and other sciences, thereby evaluating knowledge interdisciplinary in decision-making and application.
Be able to question the knowledge and skills acquired in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, and possess a critical perspective.
Analyze the algorithms and techniques required by the field of Electrical and Electronics Engineering and past data, and use intelligent sensing and prediction methods in new situations.

syllabus_topics: University, Faculty and Department introduction (introduction to student regulations)
Profession introduction, job opportunities, relevant institutions and organizations, introduction to main fields of study
Basic (SI) and derived unit systems, work, power, energy, force, Coulomb's law, current, voltage, conductor, insulator, simple electric circuit
Materials (paramagnetic, diamagnetic, ferromagnetic materials), simple magnetic circuit
Resistance circuits, types of resistors, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits, Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws
Electrical measuring devices, electrical accidents, first aid, grounding, insulation, protection devices
Introduction to semiconductors, electronic materials, and fundamentals of power electronics
Fundamentals of Power Systems (generation, transmission, distribution)
Fundamentals of programming, introduction to algorithms and programming languages
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course plan. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate decision on the dates specified in the academic calendar.
